handoff.goals: Wire browser-side PostHog identity at the authentication boundary using the app’s stable user identifier, with reset on logout.
handoff.did: No files were changed. This is a Vite React client-only app, but its only authentication is a local mock check for hard-coded `admin` credentials. `AuthContext` exposes only a boolean and accepts a username/password; it has no user record, primary key, UUID, or other stable non-PII identifier. The submitted username must not be used as a distinct ID, and adding an invented schema identifier would not represent a real application user. Consequently, no safe `identify()` call or corresponding `reset()` lifecycle exists to add.
handoff.forNextAgent: The existing `src/lib/posthog.ts` initialization is already global and exports an optional client. If a real authenticated user model is added later, call `posthog?.identify(user.id, { ...personProperties })` once immediately after successful login and when an already-authenticated user is restored, then call `posthog?.reset()` on logout. Do not use the `username` field as the distinct ID. Current app capture remains anonymous, including errors and events.

handoff.goals: Ensure uncaught browser errors reach PostHog through the JavaScript SDK’s supported global exception-autocapture mechanism, configured in one place.
handoff.did: Updated `src/lib/posthog.ts` at the existing singleton `posthogClient.init` call. Added explicit `capture_exceptions` settings with `capture_unhandled_errors` and `capture_unhandled_rejections` enabled so uncaught exceptions and rejected promises produce PostHog error-tracking events. Kept `capture_console_errors` disabled to avoid ingesting console output outside the monitoring scope. This feeds PostHog Error Tracking with globally unhandled browser failures without adding scattered manual capture calls or another SDK client.
handoff.forNextAgent: The browser SDK initialization remains centralized in `src/lib/posthog.ts` and is imported once by `src/main.tsx`. No dependency installation, build, test, lint, or app startup was performed, per this instrument-only step. A later build/review step should validate the TypeScript/Vite build and, if production bundles are minified, ensure source-map upload is addressed in deployment.
handoff.evidence: Re-read `src/lib/posthog.ts` after the edit and confirmed `posthogClient.init` contains `capture_exceptions` with unhandled errors and rejections enabled and console errors disabled. Checked the installed `posthog-js` type declarations and exception-autocapture implementation: this config is supported and enables the global listeners.
handoff.assumptions: Assumed PostHog Error Tracking is enabled/configured for the project and that this Vite React app is browser-only, as established by the upstream handoff.

handoff.goals: Select meaningful action-level events for the wedding invitation app, instrument them at the actual handlers, and record the event contract for later reporting.
handoff.did: Created `.posthog-wizard-cache/.posthog-events.json` with eight planned events. Added guarded `posthog?.capture(...)` calls to successful and failed admin login, admin logout, successful/failed invitation saves, confirmed invitation reset, venue-directions opening, and explicit background-audio play/pause. The audio event carries only the non-PII `action` property (`played` or `paused`); no submitted invitation text, credentials, venue/address data, or other user-entered values are captured. These events support a login success/failure funnel, editor save reliability and reset behavior, guest direction intent, and audio engagement. All events are intentionally personless because the preceding identity review established that the app has no safe stable user identifier.
handoff.forNextAgent: The app uses a globally initialized optional client from `src/lib/posthog.ts`, so every new capture should retain the `posthog?.capture` guard. Current authentication is a local mock credential check with no safe non-PII stable ID; all current captures are anonymous and no placeholder distinct ID was introduced. The event plan is available at `.posthog-wizard-cache/.posthog-events.json`.
handoff.evidence: Re-read each edited handler and the event-plan JSON after editing. Confirmed all eight listed snake_case events are at real submit/click handlers, imports reference the existing client module, optional guards are present, and event properties contain no PII. No builds, linters, or tests were run as required by the task.
